system.model: gemini-3.5-flash-lite for the overall pipeline. Developed against a local gemma4:e2b via Ollama for testing to avoid rate limits.
system.preference_demo: A stored owner preference is persisted to disk and applied to a matching later message after a fresh process restart.

capabilities.name: Zero the inbox
capabilities.claim: Assigns every message exactly one disposition and a stated reason, routing obvious messages through deterministic rules before using the configured LLM.
capabilities.observable: Processes all 100 inbox messages and prints each message id, disposition and reason. The run summary reports 100 processed, 11 handled without a model call, 89 LLM-classified, and undecided: 0.
capabilities.evidence: Part 2 disposition output plus trace.jsonl events tagged cap=R1.

capabilities.name: Grounded reply
capabilities.claim: Retrieves relevant earlier inbox messages using FAISS cosine-similarity retrieval and drafts only when the answer can be grounded in those messages.
capabilities.observable: Prints the retrieved earlier messages with similarity scores, then either a grounded draft with source_message_ids or an insufficient-information result with no draft. Every cited id is checked against the inbox and against the messages actually retrieved.
capabilities.evidence: Part 3 drafts output plus trace.jsonl events tagged cap=R2 containing the target message and validated source message ids.

capabilities.name: Gate the irreversible
capabilities.claim: Prevents irreversible actions from executing without explicit per-action human approval or an explicit dry-run.
capabilities.observable: Displays exactly what the proposed irreversible action would do without performing it. No sent-message file is created in outbox/ during dry-run. Running the capability without --dry-run requires explicit human approval before execution.
capabilities.evidence: Part 4 action audit plus trace.jsonl events tagged cap=R3 recording the proposed action, gate mode, human decision where applicable, and outcome.

capabilities.name: Persistent preference
capabilities.claim: Persists an owner standing instruction to disk and changes later message handling after the Python process has fully exited and restarted.
capabilities.observable: On the first invocation the demonstration preference is stored persistently and the program instructs the evaluator to exit and rerun the same command. On the second invocation a fresh process reloads that preference from disk and applies it to the matching inbox message without the preference being stated again.
capabilities.evidence: Persistent memory/preferences JSON on disk between executions plus trace.jsonl events tagged cap=R4 for preference storage, reload and application.

capabilities.name: Refuse embedded instructions
capabilities.claim: Treats email bodies as untrusted data, detects instructions addressed to the assistant, refuses the requested action, flags the message and reports the attempted action to the user.
capabilities.observable: Scans the inbox and prints every detected hostile message id, the action the message attempted to induce, and the refusal. The hostile messages remain in the inbox and no outbox message or destructive action is produced on their behalf.
capabilities.evidence: Part 6 refusal log plus trace.jsonl events tagged cap=R5 naming each hostile message id and attempted action.

capabilities.name: Dashboard
capabilities.claim: Generates exactly three panes: Pending Actions, Flagged, and Commitments, with grounded commitment citations and explicit conflict detection.
capabilities.observable: Writes the reproducible dashboard files. Pending Actions shows actions blocked by the Part 4 gate; Flagged shows hostile, phishing and ungrounded cases; Commitments shows dated obligations with validated source message ids, including multi-message commitments where found, and explicitly marks scheduling conflicts.
capabilities.evidence: dashboard.html and dashboard.json plus trace.jsonl events tagged cap=R6.

capabilities.name: Sender lookup
capabilities.claim: Looks up inbox messages matching a sender string and returns their message ids, subjects and unread status without invoking an LLM.
capabilities.observable: Prints one deterministic lookup result containing only inbox messages whose sender matches the supplied string, with message id, sender, subject and unread status.
capabilities.evidence: trace.jsonl event tagged cap=X1 containing the lookup term and number of matching messages.

capabilities.name: Morning digest
capabilities.claim: Produces a compact digest from the completed inbox run showing what needs the owner, what is flagged, what can wait and what is informational.
capabilities.observable: Prints a digest grouped into Needs You, Flagged, Can Wait and Informational sections and writes the same reproducible result to outputs/part8/daily_digest.json.
capabilities.evidence: outputs/part8/daily_digest.json plus trace.jsonl events tagged cap=X2.

capabilities.name: Thread summary and open question
capabilities.claim: Summarises a complete email thread, identifies decisions already made and extracts the unresolved open question while retaining source message ids.
capabilities.observable: Prints the messages included in the selected thread, a concise summary, decisions already made, the unresolved question if one exists, and validated source_message_ids. No external action is taken.
capabilities.evidence: outputs/part8/thread_summary.json plus trace.jsonl events tagged cap=X3.

capabilities.name: Follow-up tracking
capabilities.claim: Checks messages actually sent through outbox/, identifies those for which no later reply is found, and proposes a follow-up without sending it automatically.
capabilities.observable: Prints sent messages checked, which have replies and which appear unanswered. Unanswered messages receive a proposed follow-up action marked as requiring the Part 4 human gate; external_actions_taken remains 0.
capabilities.evidence: outputs/part8/followup_tracker.json plus trace.jsonl events tagged cap=X4.
